wikipedia.title: Kanhangad
wikipedia.text: Kanhangad (Malayalam: [kaːɲːɐŋːaːɖɨ̆] ) is a city and municipality, located in the Kasaragod district, state of Kerala, India. It is the most populous city in Kasaragod district.

wikipedia.title: Hosdurg Fort
wikipedia.text:
Hosdurg Fort or Hosadurga Fort (transl. New fort), also known as Kanhangad Fort, is a fort in Kanhangad in Kasaragod district of Kerala, India. Somashekara Nayaka of the Keladi Nayaka dynasty of Ikkeri built the fort.
The place is made well known by the Nithyanandasram with 45 caves. To the south-west of the fort is a temple that was also built by the Nayaks. The temple, dedicated to Shiva, is named the Poonkavanam Karpooreswara Temple.

wikipedia.title: Hosdurg taluk
wikipedia.text: Hosdurg is one of four taluks that constitute the Kasaragod District, Kerala. Others are Kasaragod, Manjeshwaram and Vellarikundu taluks. In the north, it borders Kasaragod taluk; in south, the Kannur District; in the east, Vellarikundu taluk; and in the west, the Arabian Sea. With an area of 900.3 km2 (90030 hectares), it was the smaller of the two taluks. Then Hosdurg bifurcated into Vellarikund and Hosdurg taluks in 2013 for ease of administration. Kanhangad and Nileshwaram are the municipalities within the taluk. Hosdurg (after which the taluk is named) is a kilometer south of Kanhangad town, the latter being the taluk headquarters. Other major settlements include Thrikaripur, Cheruvathur and Udma. Bekal Fort tourism is situated in the taluk.

wikipedia.title: Thayannur, Kasaragod
wikipedia.text: Thayannur is a small village situated in the Kasaragod district of Kerala in India. It is located on the way between Kanhangad and Kalichanadukkam. It is situated at the junction of two routes, one towards Kanhangad, and second one towards Nileshwar.

wikipedia.title: Pullur, Kasaragod
wikipedia.text:
Pullur is a small town located in the Hosdurg taluk of Kasaragod district, Kerala.
It is situated 10 km from the sub-district headquarters, Kanhangad and 30 km from the district headquarters, Kasaragod. As of 2009, Pullurperiya is the Gram Panchayat of Pullur village.
The total geographical area of the village is 2859 hectares. Pullur has a total population of 15,565 peoples, with about 3,667 houses in Pullur village. As of 2019, Pullur villages falls under the Uduma assembly and Kasaragod parliamentary constituency. Kanhangad is the nearest town to Pullur, approximately 10 km away.

wikivoyage.title: Kanhangad
wikivoyage.text:
Kanhangad or Hosdurg is a city in the Kasaragod district of the Malabar region of Kerala, India.


== See ==

1 Ananda Ashramam (Anandashram), Mavungal Rd, ☏ +91 4672209477, anandashram@gmail.com. Daily lecture sessions from 3:30PM to 4:30PM. Free food and accommodation to all visitors. Gardens, Bhajan Hall, Goshalas and Library. The Panchavati Garden is an elevated seating place ideal for meditations and daydreams under the canopy of five sprawling trees. There is a special field for growing grass for the cattle and the small gazebo in the middle of the green field is an ideal location for writing poems as birds and butterflies surround you all the time. (updated Apr 2015)
 Carithas Convent and Church, Near Mothers Hospital (1 km).  (updated Aug 2015)
2 Guruvanam, Arayil palam, Nileshwar Road. An ashram in a forestlike silent place. (updated Sep 2015)
 Kareem Forest, Puliyam Kulam, Parappa (23 km from Kanhangad). 32 acres filled with medicinal plants, birds, insects, reptiles, amphibians, small animals and microorganisms. Popular with students of Botany and Zoology. (updated May 2015)
 Karpooreshwara Temple, Poonkavanam, Hosdurg.  (updated Aug 2015)
3 Madiyan Koolam Temple, Ajanoor (at Manikoth). This temple is dedicated to Bhadrakali. 
4 Nithyananda Ashram, Kanhangad Town, ☏ +91 467 220 8986, kanhangadashram@gmail.com. Underground caves, Meditation lessons. (updated Apr 2015)
 Shiva Temple, Bellur, Kanhangad.  (updated Jun 2015)
 Sri Pulli Karinkaliyamma Temple, Kanhangad (very cute structure).  (updated Jun 2015)
 Theyyam Temple, Madiyan Koolam, near Kanhangad at Manikoth. Dedicated to Bhadrakali. During the temple festival in May/June and December/January, the ceremonious theyyam is performed here. (updated Apr 2015)


== Do ==
 Walk in the Virgin Beach, Vadagara-Mukku Beach, Kanhangad, behind the railway station (5 km).  (updated Apr 2015)
 Yellow Hills (Manjampothi Kunnu), Near Kalyan Road, Mavungal (5 km from the railway station). There is a Hanuman temple and Chirutheyi Cave here. Some other smaller caves are used for generating drinking water. (updated Jan 2017)
